zh.sourceText: 围绕青少年防沉迷，竞品平台先打出口号：不限时，才自由！某头部社交平台则强调，这一改动源于我们对未成年人保护的社会责任。第三方机构绿网观察发布的测评称，试点城市青少年深夜活跃度下降了 37%，证明限制确实有效；但该机构同时承认，样本仅来自 3 座一线城市且未公开问卷设计，结论能否推广存疑。神经科学研究者指出，单纯缩短时长未必改善睡眠质量，关键在于内容而非时长；部分教育博主也担忧，统一上限会把社交转移到更隐蔽的空间。某自媒体据此断言：40 分钟足够毁掉一代人的社交能力。在这些争议中，平台发布新规：14 岁以下用户每日使用时长被强制限制在 40 分钟以内，且晚 10 点后无法登录，超时后将自动锁定摄像头与麦克风权限。一位家长在论坛写道，孩子现在反而更珍惜那 40 分钟。平台发言人补充：我们的目标，是让每一分钟都更有质量。

textRefs.conclusion_1: 14 岁以下用户每日使用时长被强制限制在 40 分钟以内，且晚 10 点后无法登录
textRefs.reason_1: 这一改动源于我们对未成年人保护的社会责任
textRefs.reason_2: 试点城市青少年深夜活跃度下降了 37%
textRefs.distractor_1: 我们的目标，是让每一分钟都更有质量
textRefs.distractor_2: 40 分钟足够毁掉一代人的社交能力

hints: 先分清说话者：竞品、自媒体和平台各自在推什么主张？当前论证要落到哪项行动？
两条支持理由出现在政策公布之前；反对结论也混在它们与政策之间
小心：自媒体的『毁掉一代人』和竞品的『不限时才自由』也是结论，但它们是反对/竞争立场，不是本论证的理由
zh.explanation: 真正的结论是平台的管制政策「14 岁以下限 40 分钟、晚 10 点后禁登录」——这是平台希望你接受的行动主张。两条理由：①价值——『源于保护未成年人的社会责任』；②数据——『深夜活跃度下降 37%』（尽管样本存疑）。高级陷阱在于：竞品「不限时才自由」和自媒体「40 分钟足够毁掉一代人的社交能力」也是完整结论，却服务于相反立场；「让每一分钟更有质量」则是空泛标语。结论被放在争议之后，玩家必须辨认说话者和支撑关系，而不是扫第一个高亮。

en.sourceText: In the debate over teenage screen limits, a rival platform opened with the slogan: no time limits means real freedom! A leading social platform argued that this change stems from our social responsibility to protect minors. The third-party group Green Web Watch reported that in pilot cities teenage late-night activity fell by 37%, claiming the limit works; but it admitted the sample came from only 3 first-tier cities and its questionnaire was not published. Neuroscience researchers warned that duration alone may not improve sleep, while education bloggers worried that a universal cap could push social activity into hidden private chats. A self-media account then claimed: 40 minutes is enough to ruin a generation's social skills. Amid the dispute, the platform released its rule: users under 14 are forced to limit daily use to within 40 minutes, and cannot log in after 10 p.m., with camera and microphone access auto-locked after the limit. A parent wrote that the limit made conversations more deliberate. A spokesperson added: our goal is to make every minute more meaningful.

textRefs.conclusion_1: users under 14 are forced to limit daily use to within 40 minutes, and cannot log in after 10 p.m.
textRefs.reason_1: this change stems from our social responsibility to protect minors
textRefs.reason_2: in pilot cities teenage late-night activity fell by 37%
textRefs.distractor_1: our goal is to make every minute more meaningful
textRefs.distractor_2: 40 minutes is enough to ruin a generation's social skills
textRefs.distractor_3: no time limits means real freedom

hints: Separate the speakers: the rival, self-media account, and platform each push a claim — which one is the action at issue?
The two supporting reasons appear before the rule, with an opposing conclusion mixed in
Watch: the self-media 'ruin a generation' and the rival 'no limits means freedom' are also conclusions — but opposing or competing, not reasons for this argument
en.explanation: The real conclusion is the platform's rule — 'under 14 limited to 40 minutes, no login after 10 p.m.' — the action the platform wants accepted. Two reasons: ① value — 'responsibility to protect minors'; ② data — 'late-night activity fell by 37%' (though the sample is questionable). The rival's 'no limits means freedom' and self-media's 'ruin a generation' are also complete conclusions, but serve opposing positions; 'make every minute meaningful' is a vague slogan. By placing the policy after the dispute, the level requires tracking speakers and support rather than clicking the first highlight.
